map.Lessons 6-3, 6-4 & 6-5 — exponents, orde: Lessons 6-3, 6-4 & 6-5. Exponents. Order of operations. Algebraic expressions. Four reader gates stand before the second ring.
map.Previously: the vault's FIRST ring fell: Last time: the vault's FIRST ring fell to true quotients. The glitch ran one ring deeper. It is still bad at math.
map.Previously, in Axiom City: a scribble ma: Last time, in Axiom City: a scribble locked Ada Vex's code vault. It was made of broken equations. It mixed up each sign in town. The crew beat its fraction lies. Three meters of ribbon hold twelve quarter-meter strips. The first ring rolled open. Two rings to go. The glitch ran down the stairs, giggling.
map.Ring two: a giant dial of glowing powers: Ring two: a big dial of glowing powers. This is a puzzle BOSS DOOR. I have never been happier.
map.The glitch just chalked \"2⁶ = 12\" on i: The glitch just wrote "2⁶ = 12" on it. The notch went dark. It feeds the ring wrong answers.
map.The second ring is a dial of powers — li: The second ring is a dial of powers. They are small expressions like 2⁶ and 5³. Each notch glows only with its true value. The glitch reads exponents wrong. That makes each number too big.
map.Andre unrolls chalk and a plan. Mateo ho: Andre rolls out chalk and a plan. Mateo holds the lamp. The glitch yells from the dark.
map.Practice chip: 10³. Base 10, exponent 3: Test chip: 10³. Base 10, exponent 3. So three 10s multiplied. One thousand.
map.WRONG. ten times three!! THIRTY. tiny nu: WRONG. ten times three!! THIRTY. small number. so fast.
map.A power has two parts: the base — the nu: A power has two parts. The base is the number being copied. The exponent is the count of copies being MULTIPLIED. It is never base times exponent. The glitch makes that mistake every time.
map.Say 10³ \"ten to the third power.\" The: Say 10³ as "ten to the third power". The exponent counts factors. It is not a number to multiply by. 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000. The glitch says 10 × 3 = 30. That is not even close.
map.Reader — feed the first two notches thei: Reader, give the first two notches their TRUE values. The glitch wrote its little "12" on one. Write over it.
Two dark notches on the ring: 2⁶ and 5³. The glitch wrote its "answers" on them: 12 and 15. Give each notch its TRUE value.
map.Conceptual: a power is repeated MULTIPLI: Conceptual: a power is repeated MULTIPLICATION. The base is the number being copied. The exponent counts the copies. It never means base × exponent. That is the glitch's one trick.
map.Procedural: write the base again and aga: Procedural: write the base again and again with × between. Make as many copies as the exponent says. Then multiply step by step, left to right.
map.It turned one click and JAMMED. The next: It turned one click and JAMMED. The next notch is not one power. It is a whole line of math.
map.Then the line has rules. You don't read: Then the line has rules. Don't read math like a comic, left to right. You read it by RANK.
map.The order of operations: parentheses fir: The order of operations: parentheses first. Exponents second. Multiplication and division third. Do them together, left to right. Addition and subtraction last. Andre's test: 5 + 2 × 3² becomes 5 + 2 × 9. Multiplication goes next. The line ends at 23.
map.Reading 5 + 2 × 3² straight left to righ: Read 5 + 2 × 3² just left to right. It blows up to 63. The glitch loves that kind of mistake. Rank order keeps numbers true.
map.Reader — two lines, one lock. Read them: Reader, two lines, one lock. Read them by rank. Not left to right.
map.Notch III feeds the dial whole lines of: Notch III gives the dial whole lines of math. Each line must be read in the right ORDER. Then it turns. Evaluate: 4 + 3 × 2² and 36 ÷ (2 + 4) × 3.
map.Conceptual: an expression is read by RAN: Conceptual: read an expression by RANK, not left to right. Parentheses first. Then exponents. Then multiplication and division together. Then addition and subtraction at the very end.
map.Procedural: settle the parentheses, rewr: Procedural: do the parentheses. Write any power as its value. Then go left to right ONCE. Do each × and ÷ as you meet it. Addition waits for the end.
map.Two clicks down. Set into the ring: a br: Two clicks down. In the ring is a brass plate. It has Ada Vex's writing on it. Words, not numbers.
map.Word-to-symbol translation. n is the var: Words to symbols. n is the variable. It is the mystery number in a mask. I write the expressions. Reader runs them.
map.Careful — \"less than\" is sneaky. It fl: Careful. "less than" is tricky. It flips the order of what you write.
map.Andre's warm-up: \"4 more than three tim: Andre's warm-up: "4 more than three times m" becomes 3m + 4. The 3 is the coefficient. It is the number multiplying the variable. Put in m = 2. The machine gives 3 × 2 + 4 = 10. Value in, number out. That is how you evaluate.
map.An algebraic expression is math with at: An algebraic expression has at least one variable. "Times" makes a coefficient. "More than" adds after. "Less than" subtracts FROM the thing you built.
map.Reader — translate Ada's plate into symb: Reader, turn Ada's plate into symbols. Then run the machine. The glitch mouths wrong answers at you. Rude.
map.The brass plate reads: \"the key is 7 le: Read the brass plate. Pick the expression that says it in symbols. Then run it at n = 6 to get the key: "the key is 7 less than twice n."
map.Conceptual: 'less than' is sneaky — it f: Conceptual: 'less than' is tricky. It flips the order. '7 less than SOMETHING' means: build the something first. Then take 7 away from it. 'Twice' makes a coefficient of 2.
map.Procedural: two moves — write 'twice n': Procedural: two moves. Write 'twice n' as 2 times the variable. Then subtract 7 from THAT whole thing. To evaluate, swap the variable for its value. Then follow the order of operations.
map.Three clicks. One alignment left. The gl: Three clicks. One last line-up. The glitch stops yelling. It starts TOUCHING things.
map.It's rewriting the counterweight readout: It is changing the weight numbers! It just told the ring that 6² is 12. And the needle MOVED.
map.Of course it did. Every lie it writes is: Of course it did. Each lie it writes is the same lie: base times exponent. It has ONE move.
map.Analysis confirmed: the creature cannot: I checked: the thing cannot square. It multiplies the base by the exponent. Then it makes all else bigger to hide it. Use TRUE values on the last line-up. Then the ring will reject each number it touched.
map.Final alignment. Three locks: a power co: Last line-up. Three locks. A power core. A weight. And one lie that must die in public.
map.Reader takes the dial. Crew takes the sn: Reader takes the dial. Crew takes the snacks. GO.
map.Boss Gate: turn the second ring — evalua: Boss Gate: turn the second ring. Evaluate the core. Evaluate the weight. Stop the glitch's top lie for good.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. Feed the ring tr: BOSS GATE. Three locks. Feed the ring truth, and it turns. Feed it glitch math. Then we live in a vault now.
map.The glitch throws every inflated number: The glitch throws all its too-big numbers. Three locks stand before the second ring:
map.The glitch screams \"x² is x · 2!\" What: The glitch yells: "x² is x · 2!" What does x² REALLY mean?
map.Conceptual: in a term like 3x², the expo: Conceptual: look at a term like 3x². The exponent holds ONLY the variable. Square first. Then multiply by the coefficient. And parentheses are a package. Finish the inside before anything multiplies them.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — square the value of: Procedural: Lock 1: square the value of x. Then triple the result. Lock 2: add inside the parentheses. Then multiply by 5. Lock 3: think about what an exponent COUNTS.
map.The ring TURNED. Achievement unlocked. T: The ring TURNED. We did it. The glitch ran down the stairs, mad.
And look what it opened… two doors. They wear two different expressions. That can't be luck.
map.Two doors, two labels… and a riddle: are: Two doors, two labels… and a riddle. Are they secretly the SAME door?
map.Power.A base and an exponent. The base i: Power.A base and an exponent. The base is the number being copied. The exponent counts the copies being MULTIPLIED. 10³ = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000. Never 10 × 3.
map.Order of operations.Read math by rank, n: Order of operations.Read math by rank, not left to right. Parentheses. Then exponents. Then × and ÷ together, left to right. Then + and − last.
map.Variable & coefficient.A variable is a l: Variable & coefficient.A variable is a letter for a number. A coefficient is the number multiplying it. "Less than" flips the order. Build the thing first. Then subtract from it.
map.The glitch's lie.Every inflation was the: The glitch's lie.Each wrong answer was the same move: base × exponent. An exponent counts factors. x² means x · x. Case closed.
map.\"A power is a promise of repeated multi: "A power is a promise of repeated multiplication. Keep count. Then no number can grow too big on you." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 6 · Episode 2: The Power: did Unit 6 · Episode 2: The Power Ring. You know exponents. You know the order of operations. You can write and evaluate algebraic expressions.
map.Episode 3 — The Twin Doors — is waiting: Episode 3 is The Twin Doors. It waits at the foot of the stairs.
map.Andre's practice chip: 10³ — base 10, ex: Andre's test chip: 10³. Base 10, exponent 3. Say it 'ten to the third power.'
map.The exponent counts the 10s being multip: The exponent counts the 10s being multiplied: 10 × 10 × 10. Three of them. No more, no less.
map.10 × 10 = 100, then 100 × 10 = 1000. The: 10 × 10 = 100, then 100 × 10 = 1000. The glitch says 10 × 3 = 30. That is not even close.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Andre's chalk warm-up: 5 + 2 × 3². No pa: Andre's warm-up: 5 + 2 × 3². No parentheses. So the exponent goes first: 3² = 9.
map.The line now reads 5 + 2 × 9. Multiplica: The line now reads 5 + 2 × 9. Multiplication comes before addition. So 2 × 9 goes next.
map.Add last — the line settles at 23. Readi: Add last. The line ends at 23. Read it just left to right. It blows up to 63. That is glitch math.
map.Ada's practice plate: '4 more than three: Ada's test plate says: '4 more than three times m'. Start with 'three times m'. That is 3m. 3 is the coefficient. m is the variable.
map.'4 more than' adds 4 AFTER the tripling:: '4 more than' adds 4 AFTER you times by 3: 3m + 4. The words tell you what comes last.
map.Test-run it at m = 2: 3 × 2 + 4 = 10. Va: Test it at m = 2: 3 × 2 + 4 = 10. Value in, number out. The expression works like a machine.
map.Write '5 more than twice k' as symbols,: Write '5 more than twice k' as symbols. Then evaluate it at k = 3. What number comes out?
map.Night-watch drill: 2y² at y = 3. Square: Night drill: 2y² at y = 3. Square the variable first: 3 × 3 = 9. THEN the coefficient: 2 × 9 = 18. If you square (2 × 3), you get 36. That is a wrong machine.
map.4(k + 5) at k = 2: parentheses first, 2: 4(k + 5) at k = 2. Parentheses first: 2 + 5 = 7. Then 4 × 7 = 28. The 4 waits outside until the inside is done.
map.And the glitch's favorite lie, retired:: And the glitch's top lie is done: y² means y × y. An exponent counts copies of the base. It never multiplies by the exponent itself.
map.That's 2 × 6 — the glitch's signature mo: That is 2 × 6. That is the glitch's move. The exponent counts how many 2s get MULTIPLIED. Six of them. No shortcuts.
map.That's 6² — base and exponent swapped co: That is 6². The base and exponent swapped places. In 2⁶ the 2 is the base being copied.
map.Notch I stays dark. Write six 2s with ×: Notch I stays dark. Write six 2s with × between them. Multiply step by step.
map.5 × 3 is glitch math. The exponent 3 cou: 5 × 3 is glitch math. The exponent 3 counts three 5s being multiplied. It is not a number to multiply by.
Notch I glows. But Notch II stays dark. Three copies of 5, multiplied. Not added. Not times 3.
map.2⁶ = 64 and 5³ = 125 — both notches blaz: 2⁶ = 64 and 5³ = 125. Both notches glow gold. The glitch's marks burn off. The ring turns one click!
map.You added 4 + 3 first. Addition goes LAS: You added 4 + 3 first. Addition goes LAST. The exponent and the multiplication both come before it.
map.You multiplied 3 × 2 before squaring. Ex: You multiplied 3 × 2 before squaring. Exponents go BEFORE multiplication. Do 2² first.
map.Line A resists. Exponent first, then the: Line A will not turn. Exponent first. Then the multiplication. Then, at the very end, the addition.
map.You multiplied (2 + 4) × 3 before dividi: You multiplied (2 + 4) × 3 before dividing. Division and multiplication TIE. Go left to right. Divide first, THEN multiply.
map.Line A glows — line B resists. Parenthes: Line A glows. But line B will not turn. Parentheses first. Then ÷ and × left to right, in one pass.
map.A = 16 and B = 18 — both lines read in p: A = 16 and B = 18. Both lines read in the right rank. CLICK. CLICK. Two more notches glow. The ring grinds on!
map.Pick the symbol expression first — then: Pick the symbol expression first. Then run it.
map.That says 'twice n less than 7' — the su: That says 'twice n less than 7'. The subtraction got flipped. Build twice n first. THEN take 7 away from it.
map.Those parentheses subtract inside first: Those parentheses make you subtract first. That doubles (n − 7). It is not Ada's rule.
map.n² means n × n — nobody squared anything: n² means n × n. No one squared anything. 'Twice n' is the coefficient 2. It is not an exponent.
map.2n − 7 at n = 6: twice 6 is 12, minus 7: 2n − 7 at n = 6: twice 6 is 12, minus 7 is 5. The plate sinks into the ring. The key works!
map.Right symbols, wrong run — that's the fl: Right symbols, wrong run. That is the answer from the flipped expression. Double n FIRST. Then subtract 7 from the result.
map.You subtracted inside parentheses that a: You subtracted inside parentheses that are not there. Double n first. The 7 comes off at the end.
map.That's n² − 7 talking. 'Twice n' multipl: That is n² − 7 talking. 'Twice n' multiplies by 2. It never squares.
map.Swap n for 6, double it, then take 7 awa: Swap n for 6. Double it. Then take 7 away. Order of operations runs the machine.
map.Lock 1 holds. You squared (3 × 4) — but: Lock 1 holds. You squared (3 × 4). But the exponent holds ONLY the x. Square 4 first. THEN multiply by 3.
map.Lock 1 holds. x² is not x · 2. Square th: Lock 1 holds. x² is not x · 2. Square the 4. Multiply it by itself. Do that before the coefficient touches anything.
map.Lock 1 holds. Square the value of x firs: Lock 1 holds. Square the value of x first. Then multiply by the coefficient 3.
map.Lock 2 holds. That's 5 × 3 + 2 — but par: Lock 2 holds. That is 5 × 3 + 2. But parentheses are a package. Add n + 2 FIRST. Then multiply the whole thing by 5.
map.Lock 2 holds. Finish the inside of the p: Lock 2 holds. Finish the inside of the parentheses. Then let the 5 multiply the result.
map.Lock 3 waits. Tap what x² really means —: Lock 3 waits. Tap what x² really means. Say it loud so the glitch can hear.
map.Lock 3 holds. That IS the glitch's lie —: Lock 3 holds. That IS the glitch's lie. It wrote 2⁶ = 12 on the wall. An exponent counts. It does not multiply.
map.Lock 3 holds. x + x is 2x — doubling by: Lock 3 holds. x + x is 2x. That is doubling by addition. A power multiplies copies of the base.
map.Lock 3 holds. In x², the 2 sits up high: Lock 3 holds. In x², the 2 sits up high. It is an exponent that counts copies. It is not a coefficient.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Core 48, counterweight 2: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Core 48. Weight 25. The lie 'x² = x · 2' burns off the wall. The second ring TURNS. Below, two doors grind open.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
